//: Compiled against the declarations this package ships, as a consumer would.
strict and noImplicitAny are not a preference here - they are what every
project made by create-next-app turns on, and they are what turned a
non-generic useLiveEditList into forty-five errors in somebody's build.
React 18's types on purpose, because that is what a current Next app
installs and it is the stricter case: 18 only accepts ReactElement from
something used in JSX, where 19 would take a string. Checking against 19
alone would pass a package that breaks for most people.
